lines.text: You wake up on a beach. No boat. No phone. Just sand, sea — and one palm tree.
Survival runs on the rule of threes. Three hours without shelter. Three days without water. Three weeks without food. So the order matters.
First, stop. Breathe. Take stock — then salvage everything the tide gives you.
Step one: shelter. Get out of the sun, above the high-tide line — a driftwood frame, a palm-frond roof.
Step two: water. Never drink the sea — the salt dries you out faster. Catch the rain. Crack green coconuts. Build a solar still.
Step three: fire. Friction, patience, dry coconut husk — and now you have clean water, cooked food, and warmth.
Step four: food — the last priority. Crabs, shellfish, fish from the tide pools. Cook everything. Skip the mystery berries.
Step five: get seen. Spell S-O-S in rocks on the sand, and keep three fires ready to light.
Shelter. Water. Fire. Food. Signal. Do them in order — and you'll still be here when rescue comes.
